ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single triangle, with the base labeled 20, the left side labeled 19.6, and the right side labeled 16.2. The unknown angle x° is located at the lower-left corner and is the angle between the left side 19.6 and the base 20; opposite this angle is the right side 16.2. Reasoning: Use the law of cosines according to the specified method. For angle x, the adjacent sides are 19.6 and 20, and the opposite side is 16.2, so cos(x) = (19.6^2 + 20^2 - 16.2^2) / (2·19.6·20). Calculating gives 19.6^2 = 384.16, 20^2 = 400, 16.2^2 = 262.44, so cos(x) = (384.16 + 400 - 262.44) / 784 = 521.72 / 784 ≈ 0.66546. Thus x = arccos(0.66546) ≈ 48.3°, which rounded to the nearest whole degree is 48°.
